pages.title: Making Decisions
pages.content: The `if` statement lets your code make decisions. If the condition is `True`, the indented block of code runs. Python uses indentation (spaces) instead of curly braces.

pages.title: If Statement
pages.content: The code inside the `if` block only runs when the condition is True:
pages.code:
temperature = 35

if temperature > 30:
    print("It's hot outside!")
    print("Drink water.")

print("This always prints.")

pages.title: Quick Check
pages.question: What does Python use to define code blocks?
pages.explanation: Python uses indentation (typically 4 spaces) to define code blocks.
